audit.title: Data Streams Report Schema Overview

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Good — sections open with a direct claim, e.g. "Cryptocurrency streams deliver high-frequency market data for digital assets." Weak: the page opens with a bare `<DataStreams>` component and an llms.txt note rather than a one-sentence definition of what a report schema *is*.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Solid H2/H3 hierarchy, 12 headings, 0 level skips, no section over 262 words. Weak: **0 tables** on a page that is fundamentally a schema comparison — the single highest-lift structural gap.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured 0 prose numerals; "low latency" appears undefined, and "at least once per second"/"once per day" are the only cadence anchors. No field counts, no version-support matrix values, no latency figures.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 29 internal links (all schema/concept pages) — appropriate for a hub, but 0 external/primary sources. NAV, TWAP, and AMM claims could cite canonical definitions.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong instances — the ripcord ("set to true (`1`) by the asset issuer when the consumer should ignore the value") and NAV ("total assets minus the total liabilities") are crisp and liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags. Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks. A short struct/schema snippet showing field names and types per report would materially help agents; currently field names live only in prose.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers the "which schema for which asset class" decision reasonably, but has no explicit decision-phrased heading (e.g. "Which report schema should I use?") and no FAQ/troubleshooting.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming (Crypto Standard v2, RWA Advanced v11). No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a routing/index page that maps Data Streams categories (Crypto, Exchange Rate, RWA, SmartData, Tokenized Asset) to their versioned report schemas and links out to per-schema references. Its biggest strength is clean, consistent terminology and self-contained section leads that name each schema's key fields verbatim — highly liftable. Its biggest opportunity is the total absence of a comparison table plus near-zero concrete specifics (0 prose numerals, "low latency" left undefined) on a page whose entire job is "help me pick the right schema." The honest verdict: content is sound but under-structured for extraction, and metadata is absent — this is a Developing page one table and one metadata block away from Good.

recommendations.title: Add a schema comparison table
recommendations.where: Under "Stream Categories and Report Schemas," before the per-category prose.
recommendations.issue: "Each stream category uses one or more report schemas" — followed by prose only, 0 tables.
recommendations.change: Add a table with columns: Category · Schema (version) · Key fields · Best-for use case · Reference link. One row per schema (v2, v3, v3-DEX, v7, v8, v9, v10, v11).
recommendations.why: Tables are directly extractable; engines lift a single row to answer "which schema gives bid/ask for RWA?" — the page's core query.

recommendations.title: Add a decision/symptom-phrased heading
recommendations.where: Near top, above or as the category section.
recommendations.issue: No heading matches "which report schema should I use for X".
recommendations.change: Add an H2 "Which report schema should I use?" with a short bulleted decision list keyed by asset type (crypto vs DEX-liquidity token vs US equity vs tokenized equity vs staked-asset rate).
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by intent, not by "report schema overview"; concept-titled prose loses retrieval that question-titled sections win.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` + canonical + last-updated
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `about` (each schema/category), canonical URL, and a visible `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and trust; their absence is a measured, fixable defect.

recommendations.title: Quantify the vague latency/cadence claims
recommendations.issue: "at low latency" and "low latency" (measured vague quantifier), no number.
recommendations.change: State the actual figure, e.g. "sub-second (≤1s) delivery" or the true update floor, and give the RWA v11 timestamp precision as "nanosecond (`lastSeenTimestampNs`)" consistently.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes; "low latency" is unciteable.

recommendations.title: Lead each schema section with its canonical field set answer-first
recommendations.where: Each H3 (Crypto Standard v2, v3, etc.).
recommendations.issue: Field lists are embedded mid-paragraph after descriptive prose.
recommendations.change: Open each section with a one-line "Fields: `price`, `bid`, `ask`, …" statement before the explanation.
recommendations.why: Puts the liftable fact in the first sentence of each chunk, resisting skimming and parametric substitution.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal schema/struct snippet per report family
recommendations.where: Within or beside each schema section (or the comparison table).
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks; field types exist only as prose names.
recommendations.change: Add a small fenced, language-tagged block showing each report's fields and types (e.g. Solidity struct or JSON), matching the linked reference.
recommendations.why: Agents copy struct definitions; typed field lists are more reliably parsed than inline prose.

recommendations.title: Add primary-source citations for financial concepts
recommendations.change: Link TWAP and NAV to canonical definitions and keep LWBA/DEX methodology internal links as-is.
recommendations.why: Attributable claims raise citation rate; currently every reference is internal.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers on a reference page: "several," "most," "low latency" — replace with counts/figures.
Opening content is a bare `<DataStreams section="dsNotes" />` component placeholder and an llms.txt pointer rather than a canonical definition — weak first liftable chunk.
No dated/last-updated signal; freshness is unverifiable.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Site-level: confirm canonical URL emission and `TechArticle` schema are templated across `/data-streams/reference/` pages, not just here.
Establish a visible freshness cadence (dateModified) across the reference set for E-E-A-T consistency.
